item.title: More details emerge about FlyDubai co-pilot who tried to crash plane
item.description: Questions about the motive of the co-pilot who tried to crash a packed flight from Dubai to Israel continue to swirl.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: Cornell Jane Doe said she felt "like bait," documents reveal
item.description: CBS News has obtained copies of several documents related to the investigation into an alleged gang rape at a Cornell University frat house. Tom Hanson reports on the new details.

item.title: New video shows FlyDubai pilot hurt, asking for help
item.description: New video of the FlyDubai on-board stabbing shows Capt. Smit Machchhar, the pilot hailed as a hero, unlocking the cockpit door and asking for help. This allowed a small group of passengers to push in, pull up on the controls and then subdue the attacker with cords from a headset. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: Crew docks at space station with astronaut who'll miss birth of 3rd child
item.description: With the arrival of four fresh space station crew members, four others will head for home after 235 days in orbit.

item.title: New information from Title IX probe in alleged Cornell gang rape case
item.description: CBS News New York has obtained documents from Cornell University's Title IX investigation into the alleged 2024 gang rape at a fraternity party. According to those records, Jane Doe said she told the men that she was tired and didn't want to continue, but instead of stopping, she claims she was encouraged to take more substances. CBS News' crime reporter Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Trump renews threat to resume attacks on Iran after U.S. midterms
item.description: Trump said he doesn't believe "you could ever have peace" with Iran, and renewed his threat to resume U.S. attacks after the midterms.

item.title: Trump begins month-long campaign trail blitz as midterms approach
item.description: On Thursday, President Trump embarked on a 32-day campaign trail blitz to support Republicans ahead of the midterms, with stops planned for Texas and Oklahoma. CBS News' Shawna Mizelle has more.

item.title: Netanyahu says would-be plane hijacker "had been radicalized," but Iran connection uncertain
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shared more details on the ongoing investigation into the cockpit fight aboard a FlyDubai flight en route to Israel. CBS News senior foreign correspondent Imtiaz Tyab has more from Dubai.

item.title: Details on international crew aboard SpaceX rocket headed to ISS
item.description: A multi-national crew of four is on its way to the International Space Station for a six-month mission aboard the orbiting lab. They took off on Thursday to replace the 12-astronaut crew that's been there since February. Bill Harwood has more details.

item.title: Cornell rape investigation raises questions about New York's laws on consent, intoxication
item.description: The Cornell University rape investigation is putting a spotlight on what experts call a legal loophole in New York's rape laws, which makes it harder to prosecute a rape case if the victim was drunk or took drugs willingly. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Alex Gibney on his new Elon Musk documentary: "He hires great engineers"
item.description: Alex Gibney's new documentary, "Musk," hits theaters next week. Gibney joined "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Rick Ross accused of strangling, hitting woman in Miami Beach
item.description: Rapper Rick Ross was arrested by Miami Beach police Thursday on felony battery by strangulation and misdemeanor battery charges involving domestic violence.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump's firing of top federal prosecutor in Seattle
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche announced in July that President Trump had fired Roger Rogoff as the U.S. attorney in Seattle, less than an hour after he was sworn into the post.

item.title: Christa Pike's attorneys: Botched execution was "torturous" and "predictable"
item.description: Attorneys for Christa Pike, who survived an attempt by the state of Tennessee to put her to death, say they warned that her execution could be botched in exactly the way it was.

item.title: Fallout grows after Sen. Schmitt's Hawks-Hawkeyes blunder at Jack Smith hearing
item.description: Sen. Eric Schmitt mixed up college basketball teams in a high-profile moment where he tried to accuse former special counsel Jack Smith of perjury during a Senate hearing earlier this week. Republican strategist Matt Whitlock and Democratic strategist Mo Elleithee join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Homan asked about ICE killing of Renee Good as family files civil suits: "What happened was tragic"
item.description: Border Czar Tom Homan was asked about the fatal ICE shooting of Renee Good amid news that Good's family had filed civil lawsuits against several people, including Homan, for her death. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: First officer warned that Amazon plane was coming in too fast before deadly crash
item.description: The first officer of an Amazon Cargo plane that overran a runway​ last month and struck two vehicles, killing five people on the ground​, warned several times that the plane was coming in too fast during its approach, the NTSB said in its preliminary report.

item.title: 2 dead, 2 injured, 1 missing after Catalina Island helicopter crash
item.description: Rescue crews rushed to the Catalina Island coastline after a helicopter crashed in the ocean on Wednesday night.

item.title: Survivor and advocate discusses efforts to change consent laws amid Cornell case
item.description: Activist and survivor Summer Willis joins "The Takeout" to talk about the alleged 2024 Cornell rape case and her work to change the nation's consent laws.

item.title: Amber Guyger granted parole after serving 7 years for murder of Botham Jean
item.description: Guyger, who faced anywhere from five years to up to life in prison, was sentenced to 10 years.

item.title: Vance rallies for Republicans in Florida
item.description: Vice President JD Vance campaigned for midterm candidates in Florida on Thursday. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has more.

item.title: Family of Renee Good files civil suits against federal government
item.description: Civil lawsuits are now filed against the federal government on behalf of the family of Renee Good, the 37-year-old woman fatally shot in January by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in south Minneapolis.

item.title: Several questions remain as investigation into cockpit attack aboard Israel-bound flight continues
item.description: Details are still forthcoming as the investigation continues into the cockpit attack on an Israel-bound FlyDubai flight Wednesday. CBS News' Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Man who allegedly harassed Katie Miller indicted for cyberstalking in Massachusetts
item.description: The man allegedly contacted Katie Miller by phone and text over 40 times in around two months and left "disturbing messages about the victim and her husband," the Justice Department said.

item.title: Trump "trying to explain his failure" on Iran with comments to TIME, Joseph Cirincione says
item.description: In a recent interview with TIME Magazine, President Trump contradicted his previous comments on the timeline of the Iran war. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports and Joseph Cirincione, a member of the Council on Foreign Relations, joins "The Takeout" with his thoughts on Mr. Trump's interview.

item.title: "Mayday" EP on FlyDubai passenger saying show helped him during attack
item.description: Alex Bystram, the show's executive producer, said he did not expect someone to use what they saw in the series in a real-life scenario, but it was "a fantastic byproduct."

item.title: Trump lashes out about questions in TIME interview, casts doubt on Iran peace
item.description: TIME Magazine conducted an interview with President Trump recently where Mr. Trump said, "I don't think you could ever have peace" with Iran. CBS News' Weijia Jiang has more.

item.title: Christa Pike's botched execution follows a pattern of issues with lethal drugs
item.description: Death row inmate Christa Pike survived her execution in Tennessee on Wednesday, reviving debate over a pattern of botched lethal injections in the United States.

item.title: Reflecting pool vandalism charges against David Hearn permanently dismissed
item.description: In August, prosecutors asked a judge to dismiss Reflecting Pool vandalism charges against David Hearn because the damage had been caused by a contractor's "botched installation."
